symptom: `mxcli test --attach` hot-applied the injected test microflows, after which the running runtime could not load any Java class it had not loaded yet: NoClassDefFoundError caused by 'ZipException: ZipFile invalid LOC header (bad signature)'. deployment/model/bundles/project.jar was rewritten during the run (same size, new timestamp) while the runtime held it open.
cause: URLClassLoader reads entries at the offsets of the central directory it read when it opened the jar; the attach's build rewrote the file in place with new bytes, so the offsets point into a different layout.
fix: applyModelChange snapshots project.jar before the build. When the rebuilt jar holds the same entries (name, CRC-32, size), the original bytes are written back, so the runtime keeps reading the file it opened; when the classes differ, the original goes back too and the change is refused as needing a restart, as an entity change is.
insight: 'Same size, new timestamp' plus 'invalid LOC header' is the signature of a jar rewritten under an open class loader. Compare by entry CRCs, not bytes: zip timestamps make a rebuilt but identical jar differ.
test: cmd/mxcli/testrunner/jar_guard_2640_test.go (same classes, new timestamp: original bytes restored; control: a changed class is reported and the original still restored).
